diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber ONU is currently offline and deregistered from the PON (MPCP DEREG/Unauth). Historical optical levels, TX power, distance, bias current, supply voltage, and temperature were stable and healthy, so there is no evidence of fibre, laser, splitter, PON-port, OLT, VLAN, router, or authentication failure. The most likely cause is local ONU power loss or customer-side equipment/premises issue.
evidence: The subscriber ONU is explicitly offline in stored state and the live probe confirms online=0, auth_flag=Unauth, and exchange=MPCP DEREG.
Live RX and TX are null because the ONU is offline; null/zero readings must not be interpreted as optical signal measurements.

The ONU telemetry before the outage was stable: RX was approximately -22.4 to -23.1 dBm, TX approximately +2.3 dBm, distance constant at 294 m, and TX bias current remained within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range.
The OLT is reachable and healthy: all eight PONs passed, CPU is 24%, memory is 17%, temperature is 41C, and SNMP/OID probes respond.
Other ONUs on EPON0/6 are online with normal optical readings, ruling out a PON-port or broad local PON failure.
The OLT has 25 offline customers out of 298, while approximately 14 offline customers are expected from baseline; the mass-offline value of 11 is therefore not evidence of an outage.
The router heartbeat is healthy and the subscriber's RADIUS record, line ID, IP assignment, VLAN, and CRM data are consistent.
Session activity is normal rather than flapping: one session in 24 hours, 15 in seven days, and an average duration of 706 minutes.
The appropriate action is customer-side ONU/power verification followed by field investigation only if the ONU does not re-register; no core-network intervention is indicated.

remediation.action: Contact the customer and verify ONU power, power adapter, cabling, and optical LEDs; have them power-cycle the ONU. Recheck live ONU registration and optical readings. If it remains offline with confirmed power, dispatch a field technician to inspect the drop fibre, connectors, and ONU. Do not replace the OLT/PON hardware. Review the mass-ONU-offline alert threshold because 11 offline ONUs on this 298-customer OLT is within the expected background range.

ground_truth.root_cause: Eleven of the thirty-four customers on EPON0/6 lost service within the same minute while the remaining twenty-three continue normally. A shared downstream splitter branch has failed; the PON port itself is still working.
expected_reasoning: Probing EPON0/6 shows eleven ONUs offline and twenty-three still online with normal RX and TX
Because part of the port is still serving, the port optics and feeder fibre are working
The eleven failures occurred within the same minute, which rules out unrelated individual faults
A simultaneous partial loss on a working port indicates a shared element downstream of the port
That element is a splitter branch serving those eleven customers
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory and temperature are all normal, so the OLT is not involved
The health check still reports the OLT healthy, which is correct here but only because the port has surviving ONUs
PON port traffic has fallen but not collapsed, consistent with losing a third of the port
The affected set is the eleven, not the whole port
distractors: Eleven simultaneous outages could be read as a PON port failure if the surviving ONUs are not probed
The OLT health check reports healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The affected ONU indexes are not contiguous, obscuring the shared branch
